source.title: Attention Output SAEs Improve Circuit Analysis

page_placements.theme: Positional representations are structured and context-sensitive

record.tranche_reason: The study refines the proposed IOI mechanism and reports that SAE reconstruction preserves task performance in some layers but damages it in others; it also finds different mechanisms across the ABBA and BABA templates.
record.gate_note: The study tests SAE reconstruction and feature-level mechanisms on GPT-2 Small IOI prompts. It does not test the original circuit's complete 26-head structure or its faithfulness, completeness and minimality criteria, backup-head takeover, other models/checkpoints, or alternative circuit-finding methods. The cited original circuit results are not this study's results. Other recursive-DFA examples concern different behaviors and are not rows for these versions.
record.test_reason: The post's own patching, ablation and QK-decomposition results refine the roles in the original IOI circuit. Path patching confirms that induction-layer features feed the S-inhibition heads. The QK analysis shows the S-inhibition heads partly do IO-boosting on BABA prompts, and ABBA and BABA rely on different features. The SAE-splicing evaluation tests SAE quality, not the circuit's faithfulness.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct as paraphrased. Attention SAEs revealed new IOI detail: the positional signal is relative to 'and', and S-inhibition heads partly IO-boost on BABA. Reconstruction error at layer 0 and the later layers prevents a full end-to-end feature circuit, so SAEs are promising but not a silver bullet.
record.recipe_differences: Uses attention-output SAE reconstruction, SAE-feature ablation and feature path patching, plus noising tests, rather than evaluating the original 26-head circuit against its faithfulness, completeness and minimality criteria.
record.method_sensitivity: Performance preservation depends on layer: early-middle layers preserve IOI logit difference, while Layer 0 and later layers show reconstruction problems. The reported mechanism also differs between ABBA and BABA templates, and changing “and” to “alongside” reduces recovered logit difference.

fits_no_version.finding: The 'positional signal' from the induction layers encodes whether the duplicate name comes before or after 'and'. Noising that preserves this relation recovers ~93% of logit difference; changing only 'and' to 'alongside' recovers ~43%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The S2 positional signal in the GPT-2 small IOI circuit is relative to the 'and' token, not absolute or relative token position.

fits_no_version.finding: Attention-output SAEs preserve IOI logit difference at layers 1-6 but damage it at layer 0 and layers 7-11 (S-inhibition and name-mover layers).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE-based analysis of the IOI circuit is viable only for early-middle layers of GPT-2 small.

record.problems: The post describes some feature investigations as shallow; it reports no uncertainty estimates for the IOI measurements. Some layer-level numeric values are not stated in the supplied text, and the authors report substantial SAE reconstruction error in parts of the circuit.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows. The post mentions comparing SAE splicing with mean ablation from the ABC distribution, but the supplied text gives no separate numeric outcome for that comparator. The attention-score decomposition is included as r13-r14; other recursive-DFA examples concern non-IOI prompts and were excluded.

record.verdict_notes: I relinked the SAE-splicing rows from V5 to none: they test SAE fidelity, not circuit-evaluation sensitivity. I downgraded the record's V6 'challenges' to limits_scope, because the same heads are used and only feature content and sign differ by template. The recursive-DFA examples concern non-IOI behaviours and are excluded. No uncertainty estimates are reported.

versions.untested_parts: The study describes the original head-class account but does not test the full 26-head, 7-class circuit or its faithfulness, completeness and minimality criteria.
No ablation of main name-mover heads followed by a test for backup-head takeover.
No tests on other models, sizes, training checkpoints or other tasks using the IOI components.
No comparison of circuit-finding methods, ablation types or metrics for recovering the same circuit.
The study does not quantify how much of IOI behavior the original complete circuit explains, or compare the original circuit's faithfulness and completeness across prompt distributions.
It tests ABBA and BABA templates and selected prompt perturbations, but not prompts with more names or a broad range of templates.

rows.subject: GPT-2 Small
rows.operation_detail: Noised induction-layer attention outputs at the S2 position using a distribution that replaces “and” with “alongside”
rows.measure: Average logit difference recovered relative to zero-ablating the outputs at that position
rows.baseline: Zero-ablating the outputs at this position
rows.note: The post says this single change damages performance more than the three simultaneous changes in r9.
rows.check: The counterfactual 'alongside' corruption tests what the signal encodes, not whether the circuit works on 'alongside' prompts. Low recovery (~43%) is the expected result under the authors' hypothesis, so the state is observed, not partial.
